title: README.md:16 & 280-281: combined-arm calibration-sweep figure ('3 answers out of 349') has no reproducing command and 349 is arithmetically the old arm sizes
description:
README.md:16 (top-of-file summary) and README.md:280-281 ("Calibration sweep over both arms
combined") both state: best achievable precision is "~67%, on 3 answers out of 349".

349 = 175 (old/stale present-arm n) + 174 (absent-arm n). Both addends are individually
documented and tested elsewhere in this repo, and the present-arm one has been independently
confirmed stale (now 176, not 175 -- see mathgraph-3gu, mathgraph-etj, mathgraph-1f3). If the
combined-arm denominator is genuinely just present_n + absent_n, the current value should be
176 + 174 = 350, not 349.

I searched for a script or test that actually computes this combined-arm sweep (as opposed to
each arm's numbers individually, which bench_pfr.py / cmd_bench do reproduce):

  grep -n "def \|sweep\|calibrat" mathgraph/cli.py         # no sweep command
  grep -rln "calibrat" mathgraph/*.py                       # bench_dense.py, cli.py,
                                                              # freeze_bench.py, evaluate.py,
                                                              # verify.py -- none combine PFR
                                                              # present+absent into one
                                                              # precision sweep
  # evaluate.py's `sweep`/`sweep_zero_false`/`graph_arms` operate on the 439-pair non-PFR
  # blueprint corpus (idx_blueprint/idx_mathlib, see evaluate.py:95-107's own comment: "the arms
  # GRAPH_THRESHOLDS is fitted on... 439 harvested blueprint pairs"), NOT the PFR 175/176/179
  # statements this README section is about.

So there is currently no command in the codebase that reproduces "3 answers out of 349" (or
"67%") from scratch -- same class of gap as mathgraph-2zj (verify-layer table) and coupled to
the "175+174" figure baked into mathgraph/freeze_bench.py's CARD (mathgraph-q3z) and README:1105
(mathgraph task for that line), which is the same underlying pair of arm sizes.

I deliberately did NOT try to recompute "3 answers"/"67%" myself -- that requires implementing
an actual combined precision-vs-coverage sweep over both PFR arms together, which is measurement
work, not triage, and this file explicitly warns against fabricating numbers.

Work needed (whoever picks this up should choose one):
(a) Write the combined-arm sweep (likely: build `recs` the way `evaluate.sweep_zero_false` or
    `evaluate.sweep` do, but from bench_pfr's present+absent arm results together) as a
    reproducible script or test, re-run it, and update both README.md:16 and README.md:280-281
    with the new denominator (350, if it's a straight sum -- but verify precision/answer-count
    fresh rather than assuming only the denominator moved) and the resulting precision/answer
    count.
(b) If that sweep genuinely was a one-off manual analysis that isn't meant to be routinely
    reproducible, label both mentions with when/how it was produced (date, commit, or "manual
    analysis, not scripted") so a reader can tell it's a frozen measurement rather than a live
    claim.

This is the single most load-bearing negative number in the README (it's in the first paragraph
and directly supports "neither benchmark admits a trustworthy operating point" -- do NOT soften
that conclusion while fixing this; if the recomputed precision/answer-count changes, report the
new number plainly, same hedge.

Evidence that closes this: either (a) a script's output matching the updated text verbatim, or
(b) the added provenance label.
notes: Resolved via option (a): wrote combined_precision_sweep() in mathgraph/bench_pfr.py (exhaustive threshold grid over both PFR arms' pooled (coverage,margin) records, max precision tie-broken by answer count, no floor). Re-measured against idx_full/idx_mathlib (the actually-built corpora): present n=176, absent n=174, combined n=350 -- confirms the bead's 176+174=350 hypothesis exactly. Fresh sweep gives precision=1.0 (100%) on 3/3 answers, not the old ~67%/3/349. Verified the shipped GRAPH_THRESHOLDS and Aligner defaults both answer 0 on this pool (old figure wasn't 'shipped thresholds, scored'), and a zero-false-match-constrained optimum gives 75%/4 (also above 67%), so 100%/3 isn't a fluke of my tie-break rule. Updated README.md:16 and the combined-arm-sweep paragraph (~line 280) with the new number, the reproducing command, and explicit provenance for why 349 was stale (175 pre-scanner-fix present arm + 174 absent). Kept the 'no operating point that is both useful and trustworthy' hedge verbatim in substance -- 3/350 = 0.9% coverage, still not usable, argued explicitly in the handoff rather than softened. Test suite: 76 run, 1 pre-existing failure (176 != 175, known baseline), nothing else broken. Filed mathgraph-ek7 for an unrelated drift I noticed while verifying (present-arm recall@1 18.2% in README vs 18.8/18.9% measured/pinned by tests) -- did not fix, out of scope. Full detail in sandbox-handoffs/mathgraph-aec.md.
close_reason: Combined-arm sweep now exists in code (mathgraph/bench_pfr.py:combined_precision_sweep), reproducing command documented in README, both mentions (line 16, ~line 280) updated with the freshly measured 100% on 3/350 and provenance for why the old 67%/349 was stale. Evidence: script output matches README text verbatim (verified). Test suite at documented known-good state (76 run, 1 pre-existing failure).

title: README.md:250-259 PFR absent-arm section: '174 of 175' is internally inconsistent AND stale; status breakdown (167/7/0) no longer matches current run (170/4/0)
description:
README.md:250-259 ("Absent arm") has two separate, independently-confirmable problems.

1. Internal arithmetic inconsistency, visible from the text alone: line 252 says
   "only mathlib indexed, so 174 of 175 statements have no correct answer" (denominator 175,
   implying 1 statement already has an answer in mathlib alone). But the status-breakdown table
   two lines later (line 259) reads "167 unmatched, 7 ambiguous, 0 matched" -- which sums to
   174, not 175. The paragraph's own denominator doesn't match its own table's total. This is
   true regardless of what the code currently produces.

2. Current-code drift, confirmed by running the actual absent-arm evaluation with the
   thresholds the README's numbers are calibrated with (GRAPH_THRESHOLDS, matching
   tests/test_corpus.py's `Abstention` test setup exactly):

   MATHGRAPH_DATA=/workspace/mathgraph-data uv run python -c "
   from mathgraph.bench_pfr import blueprint_blocks, arm_absent
   from mathgraph.align import Aligner
   from mathgraph.index import load
   from mathgraph.cli import GRAPH_THRESHOLDS
   import os
   ART = os.path.join(os.environ['MATHGRAPH_DATA'], 'artifacts')
   blocks = blueprint_blocks('/workspace/mathgraph-data/blueprints/pfr/blueprint/src/chapter/*.tex')
   al = Aligner(load(os.path.join(ART,'idx_mathlib')), **GRAPH_THRESHOLDS)
   out = arm_absent(al, blocks)
   print('total annotated blocks:', len(blocks))
   print('absent-arm n:', out['n'], 'status:', out['status'])
   print('already answerable from mathlib alone:', len(blocks) - out['n'])
   "

   Output: total annotated blocks = 179 (matches README:250's "179 annotated statements" --
   that figure IS current and correct, leave it alone). absent-arm n = 174 (matches the sum in
   the existing status table, so "174" itself is right). status = {matched: 0, ambiguous: 4,
   unmatched: 170} -- NOT 167/7/0 as documented. already-answerable-from-mathlib-alone = 5, not
   the 1 implied by "174 of 175".

Put together: the correct current denominator for line 252 is 179 (not 175), with 5 (not 1)
already answerable from mathlib alone, and the status breakdown at line 259 should read
"170 unmatched, 4 ambiguous, 0 matched" (not "167 unmatched, 7 ambiguous, 0 matched").
correct_abstention and false_match_rate are unaffected (still 100% / 0%, confirmed in the same
run).

This is presumably the same scanner-fix corpus growth documented at README:269 for the present
arm (idx_mathlib gained ~11k declarations too, so more of the 179 statements now coincidentally
already have their declaration in mathlib alone, shrinking the true-negative count and changing
the ambiguous/unmatched split). Whoever fixes this should sanity-check that story against
git blame / the scanner-fix commit rather than taking my inference on faith -- I did not
verify why the split moved from 167/7 to 170/4, only that it has.

Fix: rewrite README.md:250-259 to say "179 annotated statements" is the pool, "5 already have
an answer in mathlib alone" (not 1), the absent arm remains n=174 (unchanged, still correct),
and update the status table to 170 unmatched / 4 ambiguous / 0 matched.

Evidence that closes this: re-run the script above and confirm every number in the updated
paragraph matches its output.
close_reason: Fixed README.md:254-262 absent-arm section: reproduced the bead's script verbatim (179 total, absent-arm n=174, status 170 unmatched/4 ambiguous/0 matched, 5 already-answerable from mathlib alone), updated prose+table to match, left correct_abstention/false_match_rate unchanged as they were confirmed unaffected. Full suite: 76 tests, exactly the one known pre-existing failure (176!=175 in test_corpus.py, unrelated). See sandbox-handoffs/mathgraph-1f3.md.

title: test_corpus.py:163 asserts stale PFR present-arm n=175; actual is 176
description:
The one pre-existing suite failure (per CLAUDE.md/handoff baseline) is real drift, not a broken corpus.

What's wrong: tests/test_corpus.py:163 (`Benchmark.test_evaluated_on_the_documented_number_of_statements`) asserts `self.got["lexical"][2] == 175`. It fails with `AssertionError: 176 != 175`.

How I confirmed it (three independent methods, all agree on 176):
1. `MATHGRAPH_DATA=/workspace/mathgraph-data uv run python -m unittest discover tests` -> fails exactly there, 75/76 otherwise pass.
2. `uv run python -c "from mathgraph.bench_pfr import main; ..."` calling `arm_present` directly against `idx_full` gives `n=176`.
3. `MATHGRAPH_DATA=/workspace/mathgraph-data uv run mathgraph bench` (the literal command QUICKSTART.md tells users to run) prints `{"lexical": {"n": 176, ...}, "+structural": {"n": 176, ...}}`.

README.md:269 already documents this: "The present arm is **176** statements as of the scanner fix below, not the 175 every table before it reports". So the test is the stale party, matching the task's framing exactly.

Fix: change the assertion at tests/test_corpus.py:163 to 176. Also update the class docstring at tests/test_corpus.py:128 ("...~0.6pt that a single statement moves at n=175...") to n=176 for consistency (1/176≈0.57%, so the "~0.6pt" tolerance rationale itself still holds, only the cited n is stale).

Do NOT touch tests/test_corpus.py:214 ("this is the 439 blueprint pairs") or any 439-based text -- that's a different corpus (non-PFR blueprint pairs), unrelated to this n.

Evidence that closes this: `MATHGRAPH_DATA=/workspace/mathgraph-data uv run python -m unittest discover tests` reports `Ran 76 tests ... OK` (zero failures).
close_reason: Fixed: test asserted stale n=175, corrected to 176 (current present arm per README.md:269 and mathgraph bench output). Full suite now 76/76 passing.

title: README.md verify-layer argmatch fire-rate table (8.6%/0.6%/0.0%) and 34.9%->41.7% pattern-augmented accept rate have no reproducing driver
description:
README.md 'Argument identity (argmatch.py)' section (~line 1045-1060) states measured fire rates (8.6% correct / 0.6% sibling / 0.0% wrong-namespace,hallucinated,random) and says wiring patterns in as an independent accept path moves the verifier's permissive/correct accept rate from 34.9% to 41.7% with every corrupted population unchanged.

Found while closing mathgraph-2zj (README:1082-1091's 5-population verify-layer accept-rate table). That table's own '34.9%' figure was the same pre-fix baseline this paragraph starts from; verify-bench (added under mathgraph-2zj, 'uv run mathgraph verify-bench') now measures 35.8% for that cell on the current 176-statement present arm, not 34.9%.

The fire-rate and 41.7%-endpoint numbers are a DIFFERENT measurement: they require the pattern-augmented accept path (Verifier.verify()'s formula-pattern branch, which only fires when math_segments is passed), whereas verify.evaluate()/cmd_verify_bench deliberately does not pass math_segments (matching the table's pre-pattern baseline). So there is no current driver that reproduces 8.6%/0.6%/0.0% or the 41.7% endpoint, and both predate the corpus's 175->176 move, same underlying drift class as mathgraph-2zj/3gu/etj.

I labeled this in README.md (near line 1045-1060) as unverified this session rather than silently updating or deleting it, per this repo's 'fix the code or fix the document' standard.

Work needed (pick one): (a) extend mathgraph/cli.py's verify-bench (or add a sibling command) to build gold_pairs with math_segments populated (see how cmd_bench/bench_pfr extract LaTeX math blocks from the PFR blueprint) and call verify.evaluate() with patterns wired, reproducing both the fire-rate breakdown and the accept-rate delta directly; or (b) if that's not feasible, convert the paragraph to an explicitly-dated/frozen measurement note like the pattern used elsewhere in this README for numbers that can't be regenerated.
notes: Extended mathgraph verify-bench with --patterns flag (builds gold pairs with math_segments, wires the pattern-accept path). Re-measured on current 176-stmt corpus: fire rate 8.5%/2.3%/0.0%/0.0%/0.0% (correct/sibling/wrong_ns/hallucinated/random), ratio ~3.7:1 not old ~14:1; permissive accept 35.8%->42.6%, precise 8.5%->16.5%; sibling false-accept also rises (9.7%->11.9% permissive, 1.1%->3.4% precise), so old 'unchanged'/'free' claims were false. Updated README.md ~1045-1074 with real numbers + repro command. Full suite: 76/76 pass. Handoff: sandbox-handoffs/mathgraph-g8x.md
close_reason: Driver added (mathgraph verify-bench --patterns) and README updated with reproduced measurements; see handoff for full before/after table.

title: README.md:1105-1106 bench_release description ('175+174 statements') cannot be verified against a real artifact -- directory doesn't exist in this repo
description:
README.md:1103-1106 ("The shipped benchmark") describes `bench_release/` as an existing,
already-frozen artifact: "`bench_release/` is the frozen, standalone version: `tasks.jsonl` (175
present-arm + 174 absent-arm statements, each naming its reference corpus), a stdlib-only
`scorer.py`, and a data card."

I checked whether this directory exists anywhere in the repo or its history:

  find /workspace -iname "*bench_release*"        # nothing
  git log --all --oneline -- bench_release/        # nothing
  git log --oneline --all -- mathgraph/freeze_bench.py   # one hit: the single initial commit
                                                          # (d64d368) that added the generator;
                                                          # never modified since

So `bench_release/` is not a checked-in artifact -- it must be generated on demand by
`mathgraph/freeze_bench.py` and distributed separately (the tool's own docstring says the point
is "used without cloning anything"). That means README.md:1105's specific counts (175/174)
cannot be checked against a real file in this checkout; I can only check them against what the
generator *would* produce if run today.

I ran the generator against the current corpus (see mathgraph-q3z for the exact repro steps --
monkeypatched blueprint path, symlinked idx_deploy/idx_mathlib_only). Result: present=176,
absent=174, not 175+174. Since freeze_bench.py hasn't been touched since the initial commit, and
the present-arm count has independently drifted from 175->176 everywhere else it's measured in
this repo (see mathgraph-3gu, mathgraph-etj, mathgraph-1f3), it's very likely that if
bench_release/ was frozen once at/near that initial commit, README:1105's "175+174" is an
accurate description of THAT frozen snapshot -- but the README doesn't say when it was frozen or
against what commit, so a reader can't tell it's historical rather than a live claim, and can't
tell whether it's still the version anyone would get by regenerating.

This is coupled to mathgraph-q3z (the freeze_bench.py CARD hardcodes the same stale 175/174) --
read that bead first, since fixing the generator changes what "regenerate and check" would even
produce.

Fix (pick one):
(a) If a real bench_release/ artifact is published/distributed elsewhere (ask a human -- I
    could not find one in this repo), get its actual tasks.jsonl and count present/absent rows
    directly, then either confirm 175/174 is correct-as-frozen-history and add a provenance note
    (commit hash or date it was frozen at), or correct the counts if it turns out to have been
    regenerated since.
(b) If no such artifact exists yet, reword README:1105 to describe what running
    `python -m mathgraph.freeze_bench` (after mathgraph-q3z is fixed) produces NOW, rather than
    asserting fixed counts.

Evidence that closes this: either the located real bench_release/tasks.jsonl's actual row counts
matching the README text (with provenance noted), or updated README text plus a note on how (a)
was ruled out.
notes: Resolved via option (b): no real bench_release/ artifact found anywhere (find + git log --all both empty, re-confirmed). freeze_bench.py confirmed untouched (mathgraph-q3z still open/unfixed, out of scope here). Reworded README.md 'The shipped benchmark' section to (1) state bench_release/ is generated on demand via 'python -m mathgraph.freeze_bench', not a checked-in frozen artifact, (2) drop the unverifiable '175 present + 174 absent' claim rather than substitute a guessed number, (3) add caveat that freeze_bench.py's CARD template doesn't recompute its counts from the corpus it's run against, so even a freshly generated bench_release/README.md's numbers can't be trusted until q3z lands -- point reader at tasks.jsonl instead. Full suite: 76/76 pass (MATHGRAPH_DATA=/workspace/mathgraph-data uv run python -m unittest discover tests), better than documented one-failure baseline because a prior uncommitted session already fixed the 175->176 test expectation. Handoff: sandbox-handoffs/mathgraph-036.md
close_reason: README reworded to stop asserting unverifiable bench_release/ counts; no real artifact exists to check them against. Evidence and full diff in sandbox-handoffs/mathgraph-036.md.

title: README.md:1029-1039 verify-layer 5-population table has no reproducing command; n=175 may need to become 176
description:
README.md's "The verification layer" section, at line 1029-1030, introduces a table
("175 statements × 5 proposal populations") with columns correct / sibling lemma same module /
same name wrong namespace / hallucinated name / random declaration and two accept-rate columns
(permissive, precise).

I traced this to `mathgraph/verify.py:181` -- `def evaluate(verifier, gold_pairs, seed=0)` --
whose `pops = ["correct", "sibling", "wrong_namespace", "hallucinated", "random"]` (verify.py:190)
exactly matches the table's row labels, and whose docstring ("corrupting gold proposals the ways
proposers actually fail") matches README:1029's wording almost verbatim. This is almost
certainly the generator.

Problem: `evaluate()` has NO caller anywhere in the repository.

  grep -rn "evaluate(\|from .verify import evaluate\|from mathgraph.verify import" mathgraph/*.py tests/*.py

returns only the function definition itself and an unrelated `NONEXISTENT, Verifier` import in
tests/test_corpus.py. It is not wired into cli.py (no `mathgraph` subcommand calls it) and no
test in tests/ calls it. So there is currently no single command that regenerates this table --
whoever measured it must have written and run a one-off script that isn't checked in.

Given every other "175" figure tied to the PFR present arm in this README has turned out to
be stale (now 176 -- see mathgraph-3gu, mathgraph-etj), this table's "175 statements" is a
strong candidate for the same drift, but I could NOT verify the actual accept-rate numbers
(34.9%/6.3%, 10.3%/1.1%, etc.) myself without writing new evaluation code, which is out of
scope for this triage session.

Work needed (whoever picks this up should choose one):
(a) Write a small driver (test or a `mathgraph` CLI subcommand, e.g. `verify-bench`) that builds
    `gold_pairs` from the PFR present-arm blocks (see `bench_pfr.blueprint_blocks` +
    `arm_present`'s gold-selection logic for the pattern) and calls `verify.evaluate()`, then
    re-run it and update the table's n and accept-rate numbers to match.
(b) If reproducing the exact historical methodology is uncertain, at minimum label the existing
    table as a frozen/undated measurement with "n=175 statements, provenance: not reproducible
    from a current command as of 2026-08" so it stops silently reading as a live claim.

Evidence that would close this: either (a) a command's output matching the updated table
verbatim, or (b) the added provenance label plus a note in this bead of exactly what was tried
and why regeneration wasn't feasible this session.
close_reason: Verified prior session's cmd_verify_bench driver, ran it (n=176, deterministic), updated README's 5-population verify-layer table with the new accept-rate numbers and a reproduce command, and labeled the adjacent 34.9%->41.7%/8.6% fire-rate claims (a different, currently-unreproducible code path) as unverified rather than silently leaving them contradicting the updated table. Filed mathgraph-g8x for that follow-up. Full suite 76/76 passing. Handoff at sandbox-handoffs/mathgraph-2zj.md.

title: mathgraph/freeze_bench.py CARD template hardcodes stale '175 + 174' instead of interpolating actual counts
description:
mathgraph/freeze_bench.py generates a standalone benchmark release (`bench_release/`): a
tasks.jsonl, scorer.py, and a data-card README.md built from the CARD string literal
(freeze_bench.py:75-133ish). `main()` (freeze_bench.py:137-167) computes the real present/absent
arm counts dynamically into `n_pres`/`n_abs` and prints them -- but writes the *static* CARD
text verbatim to bench_release/README.md, which hardcodes:

  freeze_bench.py:83   "175 + 174 statements from the blueprint..."
  freeze_bench.py:87   "- **present arm** (175): ..."
  freeze_bench.py:89   "- **absent arm** (174): ..."
  freeze_bench.py:121  "| lexical + calibrated abstention | ~0.67* | 0.011 | 0.00 |"
  freeze_bench.py:125  "*on 3 answers -- reported to show that..."

I ran the generator against the current corpus to check for a mismatch. It has a hardcoded
absolute source path (`/home/claude/pfr/blueprint/src/chapter/*.tex`, freeze_bench.py:139) that
doesn't exist in this container, so I monkeypatched only `blueprint_blocks` to point at
/workspace/mathgraph-data's copy (did not edit the file on disk) and ran main() with idx_full
and idx_mathlib symlinked to the names it expects (idx_deploy, idx_mathlib_only):

  cd /tmp/freeze_test && ln -sf .../idx_full idx_deploy && ln -sf .../idx_mathlib idx_mathlib_only
  uv --project /workspace run python -c "
  import mathgraph.freeze_bench as fb
  orig = fb.blueprint_blocks
  fb.blueprint_blocks = lambda pattern: orig('/workspace/mathgraph-data/blueprints/pfr/blueprint/src/chapter/*.tex')
  fb.main(out_dir='out2')"

Output: {"present": 176, "absent": 174, "dir": "out2"} -- and grepping the generated
out2/README.md still shows the literal hardcoded "175 + 174" / "present arm (175)" text, because
the CARD string never references n_pres/n_abs. Running this generator TODAY produces a data
card that contradicts its own tasks.jsonl (176 present-arm rows in the file, but the card claims
175).

Separately (noted for context, not the main point of this bead): the hardcoded
`/home/claude/pfr/blueprint/src/chapter/*.tex` default path in `main()` will not work standalone
in any environment other than the original author's -- worth fixing in the same pass since
anyone testing the CARD-interpolation fix will hit it immediately.

Fix: change the CARD string to interpolate `n_pres`/`n_abs` (e.g. via `CARD.format(...)` or an
f-string built after computing the counts) instead of hardcoding "175"/"174". The "~0.67*"/"on 3
answers" baseline line is a separate measured claim (see mathgraph task on README.md:16 &
280-281 combined-calibration-sweep figure, which is the same underlying number) -- decide
together whether to interpolate it too or replace it with a provenance note, since unlike
n_pres/n_abs it is not computed anywhere in this file.

Evidence that closes this: regenerate bench_release/ with the fix (using a real or symlinked
corpus) and confirm the written README.md's stated counts equal the actual row counts in the
written tasks.jsonl.
close_reason: Fixed: CARD now interpolates n_pres/n_abs via string.Template instead of hardcoding 175/174; verified generated README.md (176+174) matches actual tasks.jsonl row counts. Also fixed the hardcoded absolute default pattern path so main() runs standalone. Left the separate '~0.67*/3 answers' baseline figure as a provenance note rather than a new hardcoded number (not computed in this file; same figure is already documented in README.md as previously-stale). Full test suite: 76/76 pass. See sandbox-handoffs/mathgraph-q3z.md.

title: QUICKSTART.md:43 '+22% recall@5' structural-reranker claim uses pre-scanner-fix numbers
description:
QUICKSTART.md:43 says: "the structural reranker is worth about +22% recall@5 over lexical alone."

I recomputed the relative recall@5 gain both ways using `MATHGRAPH_DATA=/workspace/mathgraph-data uv run mathgraph bench`:

- Current corpus (n=176): lexical recall@5=0.318, structural recall@5=0.381 -> relative gain (0.381-0.318)/0.318 = 19.8%, not 22%.
- Pre-scanner-fix corpus (n=175, from README.md:930-933's explicitly-historical table): lexical 0.320, structural 0.389 -> relative gain (0.389-0.320)/0.320 = 21.6% ~= "22%".

The QUICKSTART figure matches the OLD pre-fix numbers, not the current ones -- same root cause as mathgraph-etj (QUICKSTART's bench example output), but a separate sentence/claim that needs its own edit.

Fix: either update "+22%" to "+20%" (rounding 19.8%) to match current measured numbers, or rephrase to point at the reproducing command instead of hardcoding a value that will keep drifting as mathlib grows (`uv run mathgraph bench`, compute (structural.recall@5 - lexical.recall@5) / lexical.recall@5).

Evidence that closes this: re-run `uv run mathgraph bench`, recompute the relative recall@5 gain, and confirm the QUICKSTART sentence matches (or is phrased so it can't go stale).
close_reason: Fixed: QUICKSTART.md:43 '+22%' was computed from the pre-scanner-fix n=175 corpus. Re-ran uv run mathgraph bench against current n=176 corpus, confirmed relative recall@5 gain is 19.8%, updated the sentence to +20% and pinned the formula + exact computed value so it documents its own provenance instead of drifting silently again.

title: structmatch.py:14 module docstring still says '97% ... median rank ~250', now contradicted by README's re-measured 83.5%/42

Current numbers: reach 83.5% (147/176), median rank 42 (was 97%/~250, unreproducible by any script that existed before this bead). The README's two occurrences were both updated to the new numbers with a reproduce-this pointer. structmatch.py's own module docstring (line 14) states the identical historical claim inline in code -- 'the lexical stage reaches the gold declaration 97% of the time and puts it at median rank ~250' -- and was left untouched because it's a different file than the one this bead's acceptance criteria covered (README.md:326). It now contradicts the README's corrected numbers. title: README.md:326 corpus size (242,550) in PFR benchmark section may have drifted with idx_full
description:
README.md:326 states 'the first stage reaches the gold declaration 97% of the time but places it at median rank ~250 of 242,550' as part of the PFR present-arm benchmark results (recall@1 18.2%, recall@5 31.8%, etc., reproduced via 'uv run python -m mathgraph.bench_pfr ...' per README.md:288-293).

While fixing mathgraph-zzq (README.md 'Index scale' line, a standalone index-stats sentence unrelated to any specific benchmark run), I re-measured idx_full directly and found declarations = 251,236 (not 242,550) and postings = 5,399 (not 5,609) as of 2026-08-08.

242,550 in the 'median rank ~250 of 242,550' line is presented as part of a specific, reproducible PFR benchmark result (median rank stat), not a standalone 'current index scale' fact — so it may be correctly-scoped history tied to that specific benchmark run, OR it may be current-output-that-drifted like the Index scale line was. Distinguishing the two requires re-running 'uv run python -m mathgraph.bench_pfr ...' (README.md:291-292) and checking whether the median-rank/97%-reach/242,550 figures it emits still match what's printed in the README, and if not, whether the whole present-arm table (18.2% recall@1 etc.) needs re-measuring together (like-for-like, not just swapping one number).

Out of scope for mathgraph-zzq, which only covers the standalone 'Index scale: ... declarations, ... name tokens, ... ms per lexical query' line at README.md:1162 (was :1117).
acceptance_criteria: Either: (a) bench_pfr re-run confirms the 242,550/median-rank/97% figures still match current output and the line is left alone with evidence in the bead notes, or (b) the figures have drifted and are updated together (not piecemeal) with the reproducing command's output attached, consistent with how mathgraph-zzq handled the Index scale line.
notes: Re-measured. bench_pfr had NO code producing the 97%/median-rank-250/242,550 stat at all -- it was pure prose (README + structmatch.py docstring), never backed by a script. Added mathgraph/bench_pfr.py:lexical_pool_stats() (matches StructReranker's shipped depth=10000) so this claim is now code-produced, not just asserted. Measured on current idx_full (251,236 declarations, 176 present-arm statements): reach 83.5% (147/176) at depth=10000, median rank 42 among those reached -- both a large drift from the old 97%/~250 (not attributable to corpus growth alone: corpus grew only 176 vs 175 statements / 251,236 vs 242,550 declarations, +3.6%; a scorer bug fix ('Length normalisation was backwards', already in README) is the more likely driver of the 250->42 median-rank swing). Updated both README occurrences (Why section ~L326, Structural matching section ~L958) with the new numbers, an explicit note that no prior script reproduced the old figures, and a revised claim: this is now PARTLY a retrieval problem (16.5% never reach the rerank pool), not purely a ranking problem as previously asserted outright -- did not upgrade or soften the overall negative conclusion, only corrected this one sub-claim to match measurement. Reproduce via: MATHGRAPH_DATA=/workspace/mathgraph-data uv run python -m mathgraph.bench_pfr '{"deploy": "mathgraph-data/artifacts/idx_full", "mathlib_only": "mathgraph-data/artifacts/idx_mathlib", "pattern": "mathgraph-data/blueprints/pfr/blueprint/src/chapter/*.tex", "len_pivot": 0.75, "mod_weight": 0.1, "typ_weight": 0.15, "prefix_weight": 0.85, "title_boost": 2.5}' -- read the lexical_pool field. Left structmatch.py:14's own docstring (same claim, different file) unfixed -- filed mathgraph-0a1 for it, out of this bead's scope. Full suite: 76/76 pass, 0 failures (the previously-documented 175-vs-176 baseline failure was already fixed by an earlier uncommitted session's change to test_corpus.py before I started).
close_reason: Figures had drifted (real, not just corpus-size noise) and were updated together with a new reproducing command, per acceptance criteria option (b). See notes for full evidence.

title: README.md:290-295 combined-arm reproduce command is not actually runnable as written (shell quoting bug)
description: README.md's 'Calibration sweep over both arms combined' section (added by mathgraph-aec) gives this reproduce command: 'uv run python -m mathgraph.bench_pfr' followed by a JSON argument split across three lines with a trailing backslash at the end of each line, all inside a single pair of single quotes. In bash/sh, a trailing backslash is only a line-continuation OUTSIDE quotes; inside single quotes it is a literal character and the newline is preserved literally in the resulting string. Copy-pasting the command verbatim (confirmed by extracting README.md:291-294 into a script and running it under bash) produces: json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Expecting property name enclosed in double quotes: line 1 column 105 -- the command does not run at all. Discovered while investigating mathgraph-ek7 (out of that bead's scope, which was only the present-arm recall@1 table above this section). Fix: put the JSON on one line, or restructure as a heredoc/python -c, and re-verify the command block actually reproduces combined_calibration before merging.
acceptance_criteria: Copy-pasting the exact fenced command block in README.md, unmodified, from a clean shell reproduces the documented combined_calibration output (100%, 3/350) without manual editing.
close_reason: Verified and fixed: exact fenced command block now reproduces combined_calibration (100%, 3/350) with no manual editing; test suite 76/76 pass

title: Two PFR present-arm code paths give different recall@1 (0.182 vs 0.188); test_corpus.py EXPECTED constant is stale but passes on tolerance
description: cli.cmd_bench (used by 'uv run mathgraph bench', which generates README.md's present-arm table at ~line 269) computes PFR-present lexical recall@1 via StructReranker(lam=0.0, depth=10000).rank(text, title, math, topk=5). mathgraph/bench_pfr.py's arm_present() computes the same nominal metric via Aligner.align(text, title=title, topk=5) directly, which internally uses depth=max(topk, MARGIN_TAIL)=10 (align.py:258, MARGIN_TAIL=10 at align.py:29). On the current idx_full corpus (176 present-arm statements) these disagree: mathgraph bench -> recall@1=0.182, recall@5=0.318; python -m mathgraph.bench_pfr -> recall@1=0.188, recall@5=0.318 (recall@5 identical, only recall@1 differs -- consistent with argpartition/argsort tie-breaking at the depth boundary flipping which of two near-tied candidates lands at rank 1, in around one statement). This was the entire source of the false alarm investigated and closed in mathgraph-ek7: the README table is correct and reproduces via 'uv run mathgraph bench' exactly (verified), but anyone measuring via bench_pfr.py directly gets a different, equally-reproducible number for what looks like the same metric. Separately, tests/test_corpus.py:135 pins EXPECTED['lexical']=(0.189, 0.320) -- the pre-scanner-fix (n=175) numbers -- and currently only passes test_recall_matches_published because 0.182 is within the deliberate 1pt DELTA tolerance of 0.189. mathgraph-3gu already fixed the n=175->176 assertion on line 163 but did not touch this EXPECTED tuple, so it is quietly stale and coincidentally still in-band. Suggested fix: (a) decide whether bench_pfr.arm_present should use the same depth/StructReranker pipeline as cli.cmd_bench so 'the PFR present arm recall@1' means one thing across the codebase, or document prominently that they are different pipelines; (b) refresh EXPECTED to the current measured (0.182, 0.318) / (0.193, 0.381) so the pinned test reflects live reality rather than surviving on tolerance. Not fixed as part of mathgraph-ek7 -- out of that bead's scope (which was just the README table's own number).
acceptance_criteria: Either the two code paths are unified (same depth/pipeline) with a comment explaining why, or README/code comments clearly flag that bench_pfr.py's own present/absent numbers are a distinct measurement from 'mathgraph bench'. test_corpus.py's EXPECTED reflects a current measurement, refit in the same commit as any scorer change per the class docstring's own rule.
notes: Fixed via the 'document' branch of the acceptance criteria (not 'unify' — unifying would touch align()'s shared depth default or decouple arm_present from the coverage/margin records combined_precision_sweep needs, both out of proportion to a P3 doc-mismatch bug). Verified both pipelines live: 'uv run mathgraph bench' -> lexical (0.182,0.318)/+structural(0.193,0.381), n=176; 'python -m mathgraph.bench_pfr ...' -> present.recall@1=0.188, recall@5=0.318, n=176. Added docstring to bench_pfr.arm_present and a README paragraph after the combined-arm reproduce command explaining the two are different pipelines that disagree by one statement at rank-1 due to Aligner.align's depth=10 vs StructReranker's depth=10000 tie-breaking. Refit tests/test_corpus.py Benchmark.EXPECTED from stale (0.189,0.320)/(0.200,0.389) to measured (0.182,0.318)/(0.193,0.381), since Benchmark.setUpClass uses the same depth=10000 StructReranker pipeline as cmd_bench, not bench_pfr.arm_present. Full suite: 76/76 passing, 0 failures (the one documented pre-existing failure was already fixed by mathgraph-3gu before I started). Full handoff at sandbox-handoffs/mathgraph-7dw.md. Not committed per git policy.

title: README present-arm recall@1 (18.2%) does not match code output (18.8%/18.9%)
description: While reproducing the combined-arm calibration sweep for mathgraph-aec, running mathgraph/bench_pfr.py's arm_present against idx_full with the LEX params from cli.py produced recall@1=0.188 (18.8%), matching tests/test_corpus.py's pinned EXPECTED['lexical']=(0.189, 0.320) (18.9%/32.0%, within the test's 1pt tolerance). But README.md's present-arm table (around line 265-266, 'PFR present arm' recall@1 row) documents recall@1 as 18.2%, not 18.2% vs 18.8-18.9%. recall@5 matches exactly (31.8% in README vs 0.318/0.320 measured). Only recall@1 is off by ~0.6-0.7pt -- outside rounding noise but small. Need someone to determine: (a) is 18.2% from an older/different measurement run (different corpus snapshot, different index) that should be relabeled as historical, or (b) is it現 a live claim that has drifted and needs updating to 18.8% or 18.9%. Not investigated further -- out of scope for mathgraph-aec, which only covers the combined-arm 349/67% figure at README:16 and README:280-281.
close_reason: Investigated, not a bug: README.md:269's present-arm recall@1=18.2% is the current, correct, live measurement -- it reproduces exactly via 'uv run mathgraph bench' (README's own documented reproduce command, README.md:73), which uses cli.cmd_bench's StructReranker(lam=0.0, depth=10000) pipeline. The bug report's comparison figures (18.8%, 18.9%) came from a DIFFERENT code path: mathgraph/bench_pfr.py's arm_present() calls Aligner.align() directly, which internally uses depth=MARGIN_TAIL=10 rather than 10000 -- a distinct pipeline that happens to measure 'the same' thing but isn't what generates the README table. Both numbers are independently reproducible from their own code paths; only one of them (18.2%, via the documented 'mathgraph bench' command) is what the README table claims to show, and it matches exactly. No README change needed. Filed mathgraph-7dw (the two-pipeline divergence + stale-but-in-tolerance test_corpus.py EXPECTED) and mathgraph-fr3 (README's combined-arm reproduce command is not actually copy-paste runnable) for the real issues this investigation surfaced, both out of ek7's scope. Full suite: 76/76 passing, no failures (the previously-documented 175-vs-176 failure was already fixed by mathgraph-3gu in this same working tree).

title: README.md:1117 'Index scale: 242,550 declarations, 5,609 name tokens, ~3 ms per lexical query' has drifted (currently 251,236 / 5,399 / ~7ms)
description:
README.md:1117 states: "Index scale: 242,550 declarations, 5,609 name tokens, ~3 ms per lexical
query."

I measured the current idx_full index directly:

  MATHGRAPH_DATA=/workspace/mathgraph-data uv run python -c "
  from mathgraph.index import load
  import os, time
  ART = os.path.join(os.environ['MATHGRAPH_DATA'], 'artifacts')
  art = load(os.path.join(ART, 'idx_full'))
  print('rows (declarations):', len(art['rows']))
  print('postings (name tokens):', len(art['postings']))
  from mathgraph.align import Aligner
  from mathgraph.cli import LEX
  al = Aligner(art, **{**LEX,'tau_cov':0.0,'delta_margin':0.0})
  t0=time.time()
  for _ in range(50):
      al.align('a compact subset of a Hausdorff space is closed', topk=5)
  print(f'avg query time: {(time.time()-t0)/50*1000:.2f} ms')
  "

Output: rows=251236 (declarations), postings=5399 (name tokens), avg query time=7.42 ms in this
container.

Declarations: 251,236 vs documented 242,550 -- up ~8,686 (+3.6%). This is very plausibly
ordinary corpus drift (QUICKSTART.md:108-109 already acknowledges "mathlib changes daily"),
not a bug, but the README states it as a specific hard number without a "measured as of" caveat.
Name tokens: 5,399 vs documented 5,609 -- DOWN 210 (-3.7%), which is the interesting one: more
declarations but fewer name tokens is not what naive corpus growth alone would predict, and is
worth a second look by whoever fixes this (could be a real vocabulary/tokenization change, not
just "mathlib grew").
Query time: ~7.4ms here vs documented ~3ms. I would NOT read this as drift to "fix" -- per-query
timing is hardware/container dependent and not meaningfully reproducible across environments, so
chasing this specific figure is likely not worth it; flagging only so it isn't silently copied
into the same fixed-hard-number treatment as the other two.

Fix: update the declaration/token counts to current measured values (with a "measured as of
<date>, will drift with mathlib" caveat so this doesn't need re-litigating every time mathlib
changes), and consider rewording the query-time figure to explicitly note it's
environment-dependent rather than presenting it as a precise constant.

Evidence that closes this: re-run the script above and confirm the updated numbers match (or
confirm the caveat language is in place).
close_reason: Fixed: README.md Index scale line re-measured against idx_full (251,236 declarations, 5,399 name tokens as of 2026-08-08, was 242,550/5,609) with a re-run-this-yourself caveat; query-time figure reworded rather than pinned to a new hard number since it's environment-dependent. Full 76-test suite passes (0 failures). Filed mathgraph-5hi for the adjacent README.md:326 occurrence of the old 242,550 figure, which is embedded in a separate reproducible PFR benchmark result and out of this bead's scope.
